responsibility: Register new shipments with origin, destination, and delivery deadline from controlled location lists, assign unique tracking identifiers, associate selected routes, and handle destination change/replanning triggers by requesting route reassessment. Provides the booking web/REST interface and consolidated administrative views grouped by business status (unrouted, in transit, collected). Consumes recalculated status from the Logistics Event Service rather than recomputing operational status itself.
communicates_with: Routing Service;Logistics Event Service;Shipment Tracking Service

responsibility: Compute and query candidate routes compatible with a shipment's origin, final destination, and delivery deadline; present route legs (loading/unloading points, trips, planned dates); and reassess/replan routes when destination changes or shipments deviate. Wraps the pathfinder graph-traversal subsystem. Invoked by Booking (initial routing and destination-change replanning) and by the Logistics Event Service when off-route detection requires reassessment.

Record receipt, loading, unloading, customs, and pickup events tied to an existing shipment, location, and (for loading/unloading) trip; validate and reject invalid events; and act as the authoritative owner of status recalculation, computing transport status, known location, next step, and plan adherence, and marking arrival, completion, and off-route conditions. On off-route or deviation detection, requests route reassessment from the Routing Service. Accepts events via operational REST, mobile, and periodic file processing channels using a unified event model. Booking and Tracking consume its recalculated status as read-side consumers.
communicates_with: Shipment Booking Service;Shipment Tracking Service;Routing Service

responsibility: Look up a shipment by tracking identifier to present current status, last known location, ETA, event history (distinguishing expected from off-plan events), and geographic support, reading recalculated status from the Logistics Event Service rather than recomputing it. Maintains traceability sufficient to reconstruct the shipment lifecycle including occurrence/recording times and rejected attempts, keeping a unique tracking model across all channels.
